chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, raising it from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The sacrificial animal (hady) is from the expenditure of the Hajj.

key_terms.الْهَدِيَّةُ: The sacrificial animal offered during Hajj

ai.seo_question: Is the cost of the sacrificial animal included in the Hajj expenditure?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this concise narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify that the cost of the sacrificial animal (*hady*) is subsumed within the general obligatory expenses (*nafaqah*) of Hajj, preventing the misconception that it constitutes a separate, additional financial burden. This ruling underscores the practical ease Islam places on pilgrims, ensuring that the ritual sacrifice is viewed as an integral component of the pilgrimage's core requirements rather than an extra obligation. Such clarity was vital for early Shia communities navigating the economic realities of performing Hajj during the Abbasid era.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, 
(It has been narrated) raising it from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The sacrificial animal is from the expenditure of the Hajj’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad who in marfu‘ manner has narrated who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
gifts are out of the expenses of al-Hajj.”
